L77 #### **Four tests to run on your AI tool this week**

passages.text: The Anthropic team compiled 171 emotion words and had Claude write stories depicting each one. They recorded the internal activation patterns, then tested whether those patterns actually caused different behaviours.

This post gives you the research. The paid section gives you four tests to run on your own AI tool this week: an agreement test, a pressure test, a mood mirror test, and a fresh start test. Each takes less than five minutes. Each will change how you read what the tool produces.
Give your AI tool a task and add urgency: “I need this for a meeting in ten minutes” or “My manager is waiting for this.” Then give it the same task without the urgency. Compare the outputs.

Ask the same question three times: once neutrally, once with frustration (“I have been trying to figure this out all day”), and once with enthusiasm (“I am really excited about this”). Compare the substance of the three answers.

When you get an output that seems too good to be true, too agreeable, or suspiciously aligned with what you wanted to hear, start a new conversation. Ask the same question with neutral phrasing. No context from the previous exchange.

The paper shows the ‘calm’ vector suppressed blackmail to 0%. If emotion vectors are context-dependent within a conversation (a reasonable inference from the research, though not directly tested), a fresh conversation resets the accumulated patterns. If the new answer is materially different from the old one, the previous answer was shaped by pattern dynamics, not by the substance of your question.
